title: Author + implement PROP-NNN: audit decider's close path for Mech-A verification_pattern bypass, fix the path that bypasses, retroactively annotate or close-out the 23 violation entries (ISS-2519)
background:
Integrity 02:00Z audit (monitor/integrity/report-2026-06-03T02-00.json → ISS-2519, severity=critical) found 23 entries in closed-issues.json with status=fixed, fixed_by startsWith 'decider-', verification_pattern null/missing, fixed_at >= 2026-05-25T15:00Z, and no audit_grandfathered field. Per PROP-016 Mechanism A and PROP-059 audit spec, EVERY decider self-apply close MUST write a verification_pattern (or set audit_grandfathered=true with reason). 23 violations over 9 days ≈ 2.5 incidents/day — Mech A is being bypassed at decider's close path.

Notable meta-pattern: ISS-2471 was the PRIOR tracking issue for 6 of these violations (closed 2026-05-26 by tinker fix attempt). ISS-2471 was itself closed via 'decider-verification-batch' without verification_pattern — i.e., the issue that tracked the bypass became a bypass. This is direct evidence that the previous fix attempt either missed a code path or that the verification_pattern requirement is not actually enforced anywhere in decider's logic.

Sample IDs from ISS-2519's body for tinker to start from:
  - ISS-2469 (decider-self-patch)
  - ISS-2474 (decider-archive-terminal-exps)
  - ISS-2480 (decider-selfapply-prev-run-571a3d6)
  - ISS-2511 (decider-self-apply-EXP-450-H1-wuhan-removed)
  - ISS-2512 (decider-self-apply-EXP-450-H2-aperture-sensitivity)
  - ...plus 18 more (tinker should enumerate fully from monitor/decisions/closed-issues.json + monitor/integrity/report-2026-06-03T02-00.json findings list)

The fixed_by prefixes suggest the violations cluster across multiple close-paths: decider-self-patch, decider-archive-terminal-exps, decider-self-apply, decider-selfapply-prev-run, decider-verification-batch. Either each path has the same omission, or decider's close-utility has a flag that skips verification_pattern in some modes.

operator_decision.rationale: PROP-016 Mechanism A is the audit-integrity safety net. 23 unverified closures in 9 days means we cannot retroactively confirm whether those fixes actually held. This compounds: every day the bypass continues, more closures lack verification, the audit trail rots. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs.

requested_work: Step 1 — Enumerate ALL 23 violation IDs from monitor/decisions/closed-issues.json (filter: status=fixed, fixed_by startsWith 'decider-', verification_pattern null/missing, fixed_at >= 2026-05-25T15:00Z, audit_grandfathered != true). Cross-check against monitor/integrity/report-2026-06-03T02-00.json findings list. Write the full list to the proposal file's evidence section.

Step 2 — Read monitor/prompts/decider.md and monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md to locate EVERY code path that writes a close-record to closed-issues.json. Likely paths: Step 5 patches.apply, Step 7 self-apply, Step 8 Step-A0c sweep, Step E2 curmudgeon-pop close. There may be additional paths (archive-terminal-exps, verification-batch close, etc.) — enumerate ALL of them. For each path, document whether and where it sets verification_pattern.

Step 3 — For each path that does NOT set verification_pattern, classify why:
  (a) it forgot (missing line — easy fix, add it)
  (b) it was designed not to (e.g., bulk-close paths where one verification_pattern doesn't fit all entries — needs design decision)
  (c) it sets verification_pattern but to null/empty string (still a violation — needs default)
  Operator pre-approves the following fix directions: for (a), add the verification_pattern write. For (b), either set audit_grandfathered=true with a reason field describing why the bulk-close skips per-entry verification, OR write a generic verification_pattern that documents the bulk-close pathway (e.g., 'bulk-close from curmudgeon-verify batch — see queue_id N for audit trail'). For (c), set a non-empty default with same generic pattern.

Step 4 — Author monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-mech-a-bypass-audit-fix.json. Required sections: title, problem statement (cite this directive + ISS-2519 + the full 23-ID list + per-path classification), proposed fixes (one entry per close-path with file:line and before/after), Q-OPs if any (especially around the audit_grandfathered usage if tinker thinks it's being over-stretched), verification_pattern grep (for self-validation after deploy), files_touched list, estimated_loc.

Step 5 — Tinker self-applies the prompt-level fixes per the PROP-070/072/073 pattern: write the proposal, implement in the SAME run if total prompt-edit LOC <80, verification_pattern passes (grep the fix is present in decider.md + decider-patches-and-selfapply.md), and no Q-OPs require operator review. Hold for operator review if scope grows.

Step 6 — Retroactive annotation of the 23 violations: tinker may choose either approach (operator pre-approves both):
  (a) Set audit_grandfathered=true on all 23 with reason='PROP-059 pre-audit bypass, fix-from-context inferred per closure_reason field' — fast, marks them as known-not-validated.
  (b) Re-derive a verification_pattern for each from its closure_reason text (e.g., for ISS-2511 'EXP-450 H1 wuhan-removed', a sensible verification_pattern is `grep -c 'wuhan' data/sections.json | grep -v ^0` or similar). Slower but more complete.
  Operator preference: (a) for speed — these 23 are sunk-cost audit-wise; the value is preventing future bypass. Document the choice in the proposal.

Step 7 — Lifecycle: flip PROP-NNN.json status='implemented' with implementation_commit/at/run. Flip this directive to status='completed' with prop_id_implemented set. Close ISS-2519 with closure_resolution citing the PROP + this directive + the retroactive annotation step.
Step 8 — Manually copy edited prompt files to FUSE so the next decider run picks up the fix. dome-mirror will propagate within 1h but manual sync is the safe bootstrap path.
non_goals: Do NOT change PROP-016 Mechanism A's design intent. The verification_pattern requirement stands; we are fixing decider's compliance with it, not relaxing the rule.
Do NOT add a new audit-grandfather code path beyond what already exists per CLAUDE.md DIRECTIVE-LIFECYCLE additive-edit exception pattern. Use the existing field.
Do NOT rewrite decider's close logic from scratch. Surgical additions only — every existing close-path should keep its semantics; we are adding the missing field write.

Do NOT scope to fixing the FUSE-revert incident in this directive. That is a SEPARATE concern filed as DIRECTIVE-20260603-002. The two share a surface (decider close-path + sync race) but the fixes are independent.

Do NOT block on retroactive annotation (Step 6) — if tinker runs out of LOC budget, ship Steps 1-5 + 7-8 and queue Step 6 as a follow-up tinker run. The forward-looking fix is more important than the historical cleanup.

expected_output: (1) monitor/tinker/proposals/PROP-NNN-mech-a-bypass-audit-fix.json with status='implemented'. (2) Edits to monitor/prompts/decider.md and/or monitor/prompts/reference/decider-patches-and-selfapply.md adding verification_pattern writes at every close-path that was missing it. (3) Either (Step 6a) bulk audit_grandfathered=true annotation on the 23 violation entries in closed-issues.json, OR (Step 6b) per-entry verification_pattern backfill. (4) ISS-2519 closed in open-issues.json with closure_resolution citing PROP-NNN + this directive. (5) This directive at status='completed'. (6) FUSE-synced prompt edits.

Implementation (Step 5, ~15 min — should be <50 lines across 2-3 files). Retroactive annotation Step 6a is mechanical (~10 min) or Step 6b is per-entry-thinking (~30 min). Lifecycle (Step 7-8, ~10 min).
priority_note: HIGH — critical severity from integrity audit, recurring violation pattern (~2.5/day), audit-trail integrity issue. Worth shipping in the next 1-2 tinker runs even if it pushes other lower-priority work.
